principles: Prefer fixing the stale test assumption over changing correct production logic
Repro-first: every fix is preceded by a committed RED script that fails on the pre-fix tree
Minimal, targeted diffs -- no unrelated refactors or scope creep into Authority Server / PROCESS_FACT_REGISTRY redesign
Leave a clear registration decision (validate.commands) so this class of regression cannot go silent again
Preserve each fixture's original discriminating intent (do not just silence the assertion)
drivers: All three failures are fixture-side staleness relative to correct, intentional production changes -- production code should not be weakened to accommodate stale fixtures
None of the three fixtures are in lattice.config.json validate.commands, so this class of regression is currently invisible to the standard REVIEW/validate loop
User explicitly required repro-first (RED before GREEN) for each of the three, bundled into one story driven to DONE

options.name: Fixture-only fixes (update stale synthetic setup in each fixture)
pros: Smallest possible diff; zero risk to real production behavior
Directly addresses the confirmed root cause in all three cases (fixture assumptions predate real registry/schema/version-bump changes)
cons: If worktree-authority-smoke.ts's root cause turns out to need done_recover itself to handle a missing package.json more gracefully in real partial-DONE recovery scenarios (not just this fixture), a fixture-only fix would paper over a genuine production gap

options.name: Fixture fixes plus defensive production hardening
pros: Covers the fixture-only case AND any latent production robustness gap in bumpVersionOnDoneMerge/done_recover
cons: Larger diff and larger REVIEW surface for a story whose confirmed root causes (checked directly against source) are fixture staleness, not production bugs
Risk of scope creep beyond what was actually confirmed by investigation

chosen: Fixture-only fixes (update stale synthetic setup in each fixture)
rationale: Direct source investigation (buildBoundedSourceGraph, command-catalog.ts required readManifest, bumpVersionOnDoneMerge's package.json requirement) confirmed all three production code paths are behaving exactly as intended; the fixtures are stale relative to legitimate prior changes. CHK-003's DEV work will attempt the fixture-only fix first per the recorded unknown, and only touch production code if that investigation surfaces a genuine gap.

preMortem.scenario: The fixture-only fix for worktree-authority-smoke.ts (stubbing package.json in the synthetic root) makes the RED script pass but masks a real gap where done_recover crashes on genuine partial-DONE recoveries whose worktree predates the version-bump feature
preMortem.trigger: A real partial-DONE recovery on an older worktree lacking expected version sync-point files
preMortem.consequence: done_recover throws in production exactly like the fixture did, but now with no test coverage catching it since the fixture was fixed to avoid the exact condition
preMortem.mitigation: During DEV, explicitly check whether bumpVersionOnDoneMerge already has a defined behavior for a pre-version-bump-era worktree (e.g. an existence check or version marker); if none exists, escalate to the two-option decision (fixture-only vs defensive hardening) instead of silently choosing fixture-only

preMortem.scenario: Adding the two missing stub files to proofstory-acceptance-basis-smoke.ts's writeCanonicalAcceptanceRegistration accidentally changes the semantic content in a way that makes the fixture pass vacuously (e.g. stub content that trivially satisfies every adapter) rather than genuinely re-proving the intended acceptance-basis invariant
preMortem.trigger: Copy-pasting an existing stub's shape without checking what each new file's real production counterpart's structural role actually is
preMortem.consequence: The fixture goes green but stops discriminating a genuine future regression in the acceptance-rollout closure logic
preMortem.mitigation: After the fix, deliberately break the fix (revert the new stub content) and confirm the fixture fails again with the original snapshot_missing error, proving the fixture still has real discriminating power

preMortem.scenario: Fixing field-regression-cli-smoke.ts's --readManifest argument by passing an empty or trivial object makes the CLI call succeed but the fixture's original staleness assertion (/already stale|stale/i) never actually gets exercised because the new readManifest happens to avoid the staleness code path entirely
preMortem.trigger: Constructing a minimal readManifest object just to satisfy the required-field validator, without checking what shape actually triggers the staleness branch being tested
preMortem.consequence: The fixture passes but silently stops testing the staleness scenario it was written for, identical in kind to F-002/F-003/F-004's non-discriminating-evidence class from B-a7c5
preMortem.mitigation: Match the readManifest shape used by other currently-passing tests that exercise the same staleness code path (per CHK-002's context), and confirm the fixed fixture's assertion actually matches against real 'already stale' output, not just against any non-crashing output

preMortem.scenario: Registering one or more of the three fixtures into lattice.config.json validate.commands (CHK-004) introduces flakiness or excessive runtime into the concurrent validate suite, since worktree-authority-smoke.ts and field-regression-cli-smoke.ts spawn real git repos and CLI subprocesses
preMortem.trigger: Adding all three unconditionally without checking their runtime cost or concurrency-safety against the rest of validate.commands
preMortem.consequence: lattice validate becomes slower or intermittently flaky for every story in the repo, a much broader blast radius than this story's actual bug fixes
preMortem.mitigation: CHK-004 explicitly evaluates and records a per-fixture registration decision rather than blanket-registering all three; only register a fixture if its runtime/isolation profile matches other validate.commands entries of similar shape (e.g. other worktree-spawning smoke tests already in that list)
